questions.prompt: Why can you download, change, and republish most federal data without permission?
choices: Works made by U.S. government employees are not protected by copyright
Federal data carry a Creative Commons license
Federal agencies sell unlimited licenses to universities
Data are facts, so no data are ever copyrighted
questions.explain: Under 17 U.S.C. § 105, works of the U.S. government are in the public domain. Check the use constraints anyway: some data sets include partners' data.

questions.prompt: Because federal data are public domain, you don't need to cite them.
questions.explain: Good practice, and most agencies, ask you to cite the agency, product, version, and access date.

questions.prompt: Which is NOT a usual advantage of federal data sets?
choices: They are always the newest and most detailed data for any place
They cover the whole country with one method
questions.explain: State and local data are often newer or finer, such as North Carolina's flood maps and lidar. Always check for them.

questions.prompt: Which federal data set is a legal, regulatory boundary rather than just a map?
questions.explain: Flood Insurance Rate Maps decide who must buy flood insurance, and change only through a formal process.

questions.prompt: Which portal is the main place to download 3DEP elevation, NHD streams, and watershed boundaries?
questions.explain: The USGS National Map Downloader serves elevation, hydrography, boundaries, and US Topo maps.

questions.prompt: Where would you search for MODIS and VIIRS products?
questions.explain: NASA's Earthdata Search finds data from every NASA archive, with one free Earthdata Login.

questions.prompt: NAIP aerial photography is run by:
questions.explain: NAIP is run by USDA's Aerial Photography Field Office, to check compliance with farm programs.

questions.prompt: Which bands does recent NAIP imagery have?
questions.explain: The near-infrared band lets you make false-color images and NDVI at sub-meter resolution.

questions.prompt: NAIP is flown leaf-on. What does that make it poor at?
choices: Seeing the ground, streams, and sidewalks under trees
questions.explain: Leaf-on photos are great for vegetation, but the canopy hides what is beneath it.

questions.prompt: How many 60 cm NAIP pixels fit in one 30 × 30 m Landsat pixel?
If you halve the pixel size of a raster, the number of pixels covering the same area:
questions.explain: Pixel count rises with the square of the resolution: half the size in each direction makes 2 × 2 = 4 times as many.

questions.prompt: You need to map individual sidewalks on campus. Which data set fits best?
questions.explain: Sidewalks are a few meters wide, so they need sub-meter imagery such as NAIP. 30 m pixels can't show them.

questions.prompt: NLCD land cover is classified from:
questions.explain: NLCD's 30 m cells match Landsat's, from which it is classified.

questions.prompt: NLCD's four developed classes are defined by:
choices: The percentage of impervious surface in each cell
questions.explain: Open space has under 20 percent impervious surface; low 20–49; medium 50–79; high 80–100.

questions.prompt: Most of NLCD's 'Developed, Open Space' class is:
choices: Lawns, golf courses, and grassy road margins
questions.explain: Open space has under 20 percent impervious surface. It is not the same as parkland.

questions.prompt: In NLCD's two-digit codes, what does a first digit of 4 mean?
questions.explain: 1 is water, 2 developed, 4 forest, 8 agriculture, and 9 wetlands. 41 is deciduous forest.

questions.prompt: For a change study, it is fine to compare a classic NLCD edition with an Annual NLCD map.
questions.explain: Mixing products mixes methods, so the 'change' may be a change in method. Use the Annual NLCD for every year.

questions.prompt: Which NLCD classes are most often confused with each other?
choices: Grassland and pasture, and the kinds of wetland
questions.explain: Classes that look alike from space are confused most. Water and developed land are mapped reliably.

questions.prompt: Why should you keep NLCD in its Albers Equal Area projection when measuring land cover area?
choices: Every cell then has the same area
It is the only projection QGIS can read
questions.explain: In an equal-area projection, cell counts convert directly to area. In geographic coordinates, cell areas vary with latitude.

questions.prompt: What happened to the Landsat archive in 2008?
choices: It was opened for free download
It was sold to a private company
It was moved to the European Space Agency
questions.explain: Free access sent downloads from thousands of scenes a year to millions.

questions.prompt: What is the resolution of Landsat 8 and 9's multispectral bands?
questions.explain: 30 m multispectral, 15 m panchromatic, and 100 m thermal.

questions.prompt: Together, Landsat 8 and 9 image the same place every how many days?
questions.explain: Each satellite revisits every 16 days; offset from each other, they give one image every 8 days.

questions.prompt: In a false color infrared image, which band is shown in the red channel?
questions.explain: Near-infrared goes into red, so healthy vegetation, which reflects NIR strongly, looks bright red.

questions.prompt: A cell reflects 0.05 of red light and 0.45 of near-infrared light. What is its NDVI?
Which surface usually has a negative NDVI?
questions.explain: Water reflects less near-infrared than red, so NIR − Red is negative.

questions.prompt: What does MODIS trade for its daily images of the whole Earth?
choices: Spatial detail: its pixels are 250 m to 1 km
Spectral detail: it has only one band
Coverage: it images only the United States
Cost: its data must be bought
questions.explain: Coarse pixels, frequent images: ideal for phenology, drought, fire, and snow over large areas.

questions.prompt: Which NASA tool clips MODIS, VIIRS, or Landsat products to your own area and dates?
questions.explain: AppEEARS returns just your area and dates as GeoTIFFs or a CSV.

questions.prompt: Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 (HLS) gives:
choices: 30 m surface reflectance every 2 to 3 days
questions.explain: Combining Landsat 8 and 9 with Europe's Sentinel-2 satellites fills in the gaps between Landsat passes.

questions.prompt: 3DEP's Quality Level 2 lidar has a vertical accuracy of about:
questions.explain: QL2 is about 2 points per square meter with 10 cm vertical accuracy.

questions.prompt: The seamless 3DEP DEMs are never updated after release, so the download date doesn't matter.
questions.explain: They are updated as each new lidar project is added, so always record the date.

questions.prompt: What lets a GIS trace water downstream through the NHD?
choices: Flowlines carry a flow direction and reach code
questions.explain: NHD flowlines form a network with flow direction.

questions.prompt: How many digits are in the code of a HUC subbasin, the level whose code for the Haw River is 03030002?
questions.explain: A HUC-8 subbasin has 8 digits; each level adds two.

questions.prompt: Put the hydrologic units in order, from largest to smallest.
questions.explain: Each level adds two digits and nests inside the one above.

questions.prompt: In a map of WBD boundaries over a hillshade, HUC-12 boundaries follow:
questions.explain: A watershed is the land draining to one outlet, so its edge runs along the divides.

questions.prompt: FEMA's Special Flood Hazard Area is the land flooded by:
choices: Any flood in the last 100 years
questions.explain: The 1 percent annual chance, or '100-year,' flood. Zones begin with A or V.

questions.prompt: What does Zone AE have that Zone A does not?
questions.explain: Zone A has no detailed study and no base flood elevation; AE has one; VE adds waves.

questions.prompt: Shaded Zone X on a FIRM marks:
choices: Areas with no flood risk at all
questions.explain: Shaded X is the '500-year' floodplain. Unshaded X is minimal hazard, which is not no hazard.

questions.prompt: The regulatory floodway is:
choices: The channel and nearby floodplain that must stay open to carry flood flows
Land above the base flood elevation
questions.explain: Building in the floodway must not raise flood heights.

questions.prompt: To the nearest whole percent, what is the chance of at least one 1 percent annual chance flood in 30 years?
After a 100-year flood, the next one can't come for about a century.
questions.explain: It has a 1 percent chance every year, independent of past years. Two can happen in back-to-back years.

questions.prompt: Which three parts does the National Risk Index combine?
choices: Expected annual loss, social vulnerability, and community resilience
questions.explain: Risk rises with expected loss and social vulnerability, and falls with resilience.

questions.prompt: How do you attach National Risk Index scores to census tract boundaries?
questions.explain: NRI tables carry the GEOID, so they join directly to census data and boundaries.

questions.prompt: The National Risk Index is designed to assess the flood risk of a single building.
questions.explain: It is a screening tool for comparing places, not a site-level risk assessment.

questions.prompt: A state's 303(d) list is a list of:
choices: Impaired waters that need pollution cut
questions.explain: Section 303(d) of the Clean Water Act requires states to list impaired waters.

questions.prompt: Which EPA tool gives plain-language water quality information for any address?
questions.explain: How's My Waterway is built on ATTAINS and WATERS, which link state assessments to NHDPlus.

questions.prompt: A stream that has not been assessed can be assumed to be clean.
questions.explain: Not assessed is not clean. Most stream miles have never been assessed.

questions.prompt: You need to track floodwater across eastern North Carolina every few days after a hurricane. Which fits best?
questions.explain: Fast-changing events need frequent images; accept coarser pixels.

questions.prompt: You need to measure forest lost to development in a county from 2000 to 2020. Which fits best?
questions.explain: The Annual NLCD maps every year with one method, so you can measure change consistently.

questions.prompt: 3DEP's seamless DEM is in NAD83 geographic coordinates and NLCD in Albers Equal Area. Before overlaying them you should:
choices: Project them to a common coordinate system
Nothing; the GIS ignores coordinate systems
questions.explain: Project to a common CRS before overlay, ideally an equal-area one when measuring area.

questions.prompt: Which habit protects your project if a federal portal is redesigned or a data set is withdrawn?
choices: Keep a local copy and record the version and access date
Link to the portal's home page
Download again each time you need it
questions.explain: Federal sites and products change. Save what you used and write down where it came from.
